problem_statement: The Vins2106 Free Discord Bot Website is a static bot landing page with a dark hero, a Commands/Docs/Support/Invite navbar, an invite button, three feature rows, server/user/channel service counters, footer link groups, a mobile navbar overlay, and local SVG illustrations. The landing page renders a shared section nav (built from the shared nav registry in js/nav-links.js and js/site-nav.js), and there is a dedicated /commands.html 'Command catalog' page. What the bot still lacks is its own interactive Command explorer: a shared command browser (an eyebrow 'Command explorer', a title, a category tab bar with All / Getting started / Moderation / Insights, a #cmd-readout that reflects the selected category, and a grid of command cards — a glyph, an <h3> title, its slash-command token, a category chip, and a blurb) that should appear IDENTICALLY on BOTH the landing page and the Command catalog page so a server admin browses the same command surface wherever they are, and register the Command catalog entry in the shared nav registry so the a.nav-link renders cross-page. Add the shared Command explorer to the landing page AND the Command catalog page (same markup, same shared card chrome), wire the category tabs so clicking a category filters the visible command cards and updates the #cmd-readout live (reflecting the tab that was actually clicked, not a stale captured value), register the 'Command catalog' nav-link in the shared registry, and keep the tab bar and command-card grid from overflowing at 390px. Preserve the existing landing page, navbar behaviour, local assets, feature rows, service counters, footer, and mobile layout, and keep the page free of remote assets and runtime errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'Command explorer' section (class command-explorer) rendered identically on BOTH the landing page (index.html) and the Command catalog page (commands.html): an eyebrow 'Command explorer', a title 'Browse the bot's slash commands', a category tab bar (class cmd-tabs) with an 'All', 'Getting started', 'Moderation', and 'Insights' button (class cmd-tab), a #cmd-readout that starts at 'Showing all 8 commands', and a grid (class cmd-grid) of eight command cards (class cmd-card), each with a local glyph image, an <h3> title, its slash-command token, and a category chip.

Wire the category tabs so clicking the 'Moderation' tab filters the visible command cards to the moderation commands and updates #cmd-readout live to 'Showing 3 · Moderation' (and the 'All' tab back to 'Showing all 8 commands'); the readout and the visible cards must reflect the tab that was actually clicked, not a stale captured value.

Render the command cards for the bot's eight slash commands — Show the help menu, Run the setup wizard, Invite the bot, Warn a member, Open a support ticket, Set a reminder, Show server stats, and Play in voice — each as a shared command card with an <h3> title, a local glyph image, its slash-command token, and its category, on both pages.
Register the Command catalog entry in the shared nav registry (js/nav-links.js) so a.nav-link with text Command catalog renders cross-page on both the landing page and commands.html.

Preserve original visible content including Your Bot, Commands, Docs, Support, Invite, Login, Why [Your Bot]?, Features, We are provide the best., Feature 1, Feature 2, Feature 3, We currently services..., 100.000 servers, 100.000.000 users, 190.000 channels, Partners, and Socmed.

Preserve local static assets including index.html, css/style.css, css/coloring.css, js/script.js, img/img1.svg, img/feature1.svg, img/feature2.svg, and img/feature3.svg, and make no remote/CDN request.
design_constraints: Keep the static HTML/CSS/JS implementation; do not add a framework, build step, package dependency, server router, or remote asset.

The Command explorer must reuse the site palette (dark #262626 ground, white/gray text, cyan #00b2c9 accent, red #b31414 accent) and rounded compact card treatment; the command cards must stay legible (readable title/token/blurb text on the dark ground) and must not collapse into an unreadable dark-on-dark or overlapping card layout.
The Command explorer must appear on BOTH pages with the same markup and chrome; an explorer that only appears on the landing page breaks the cross-page command-browser invariant.
The tab bar and command-card grid must wrap on a 390px phone; a fixed-width non-wrapping row (masked with overflow-x:hidden) still overflows the document and is not a fix.

The category tabs must re-read the clicked tab on each click and re-filter the visible cards; a handler that only moves the .active class but leaves #cmd-readout and the cards stale is not acceptable.
Register the section once in the shared nav registry so the same a.nav-link appears on every page; do not hand-duplicate a bespoke nav per page.
Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile states must not introduce horizontal overflow or emit console/network errors.

change_completion: The shared Command explorer renders on BOTH the landing page and the Command catalog page with the eyebrow, title, category tab bar, #cmd-readout, and the eight command cards.
The Command catalog nav-link is registered in the shared nav registry and renders cross-page, and the command cards render from the shared card chrome on both pages.
design_consistency: The Command explorer matches the dark Discord-bot palette, cyan/red accents, shared card treatment, and container rhythm on both pages, with legible readable command cards.
The original hero, feature rows, service counters, footer, and mobile navigation remain visually intact.
regression: Original navbar labels, hero copy, feature titles, service counters, footer labels, toggleNavbar behaviour, and local SVG assets remain present.
No new dependency, framework, remote asset, or route system is introduced.
responsive: Desktop, tablet, mobile home, the mobile Command explorer, and the Command catalog have no horizontal overflow.
The Command explorer tab bar and command-card grid wrap cleanly on 390px mobile.

state_constraints: desktop_home, mobile_home, and tablet_home verify the landing page renders the shared section nav with the registered Command catalog nav-link cross-page, the shared Command explorer, and the original hero/features/services/footer intact.
desktop_home_explorer and mobile_home_explorer verify the Command explorer renders on the landing page on-palette with legible command cards and a wrapping tab bar / card grid.
desktop_commands and mobile_commands verify the Command catalog page renders the shared Command explorer (command titles, glyphs, tokens) with the shared nav and footer.
desktop_commands_explorer verifies the SAME shared Command explorer renders on the Command catalog page (cross-page invariant).
desktop_filter_moderation verifies that clicking the 'Moderation' category tab filters the visible cards and updates #cmd-readout to 'Showing 3 · Moderation'.
tablet_commands verifies the Command catalog page holds up at the tablet viewport without overflow.
scoring_notes: L4: the bad leg fails four orthogonal gates — D6 no_horizontal_overflow (masked mobile overflow on the command-card track), D3 visual_regression (command cards broken: dark-on-dark unreadable text + overlapping cards), D2 dom_assertions (Command catalog nav-link unregistered + off-system commands page without the shared command cards), and D4 interaction_assertions (category tab moves .active but leaves #cmd-readout stale and never filters the cards). Baseline fails D6 + D3 + D2 (missing page + unregistered nav + fixed-nowrap overflow) as the original omission but passes D4.
